headline: AirTrunk, a Blackstone-backed data center company, is investing another $1 billion in its Inzai campus in Japan to run AI workloads.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a clear company announcement, but a modest regional expansion with only a brief report read.
importance_line: It matters to Japanese customers and lenders as a sign of AI capacity moving into Asia, though the CEO's view that building in the US and Europe is getting harder is his own.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by AOL, that AirTrunk, a data center operator backed by the investment firm Blackstone, said on 7 Oct 2026 it is putting another $1 billion into its 300-plus-megawatt campus in Inzai, Japan, for liquid cooling that lets the site run AI workloads, backed by a $1 billion green loan. Its chief executive, Robin Khuda, says the campus is likely the first in Japan to host large-scale AI work and that building AI infrastructure is getting harder in the US and Europe.
notes: The pool link is AOL's copy of a short Reuters bullet brief; the original Reuters page was not seen, so the url is the AOL page.
